'''Diacetonamine''' is a useful precursor in organic synthesis.

Diacetonamine and [[triacetonamine]] are formed in plant extracts:<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Stewart, I.)), ((Wheaton, T. A.)) | journal=Phytochemistry | title=Formation of diacetonamine and triacetonamine in plant extracts | volume=6 | issue=11 | pages=1587–1588 | date= November 1967 | doi=10.1016/S0031-9422(00)82956-8 | bibcode=1967PChem...6.1587S }}</ref>

Diacetonamine contains an acetyl group, a primary amine, and two methyl groups.
==Applications==
It is known to have application in the synthesis of [[eucaine]]<ref name=Lednicer>{{cite book | vauthors=((Lednicer, D.)), ((Mitscher, L. A.)) | date= 1977 | title=The organic chemistry of drug synthesis. 1 | publisher=Wiley | isbn=9780471521419}}</ref> & [[alpha-eucaine]].<ref name=Lednicer/>
[[File:6-(4-Chlorophenyl)-2,2-dimethylpiperidin-4-one.svg|center|151px]]
Additionally it was used in the synthesis of [2104-81-6], an agent discovered by [[C. Robin Ganellin]].<ref name=piperidone>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Ganellin, C. R.)), ((Spickett, R. G. W.)) | journal=Journal of Medicinal Chemistry | title=Compounds Affecting the Central Nervous System. I. 4-Piperidones and Related Compounds | volume=8 | issue=5 | pages=619–625 | date= September 1965 | doi=10.1021/jm00329a015 | pmid=5867943 }}</ref><ref>Ganellin Charon Robin & Spickett Robert Geoffr William, {{US patent|3067204}} (1962 to Smith Kline and French Laboratories Ltd).</ref> This compound has [[central nervous system]] activity as a combination of a stimulant and a depressant. A narcotic pharmacophore was associated with the structure in an earlier work.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Anker, R. M.)), ((Cook, A. H.)), ((Heilbron, I. M.)) | journal=Journal of the Chemical Society (Resumed) | title=240. Experiments in the piperidine series. Part II | pages=917 | date= 1945 | doi=10.1039/jr9450000917}}</ref>

Another place that diacetonamine is used is in the synthesis of [[Eucatropine]] (euphtalmin) [100-91-4].<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Kipping, F. S.)) | journal=J. Chem. Soc., Trans. | title=CCCLXVIII.—Some derivatives of the vinyldiacetonalkamines | volume=123 | pages=3115–3119 | date= 1923 | doi=10.1039/CT9232303115}}</ref> The synthesis route is ''via'' the precursor 2,2,6-trimethylpiperidin-4-one [3311-23-7].<ref>[https://www.prepchem.com/synthesis-of-226-trimethylpiperidin-4-one/ Organic medical chemicals, by M. Barrowliff, 98, 1921.]</ref> This is the same chemical as was used in the synthesis of beta-eucaine (see above).

==Synthesis==
It is formed by the [[conjugate addition]] of ammonia to [[mesityl oxide]].<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Haeseler, P. R.)) | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | title=Preparation of Diacetonamine. | volume=47 | issue=4 | pages=1195–1196 | date= April 1925 | doi=10.1021/ja01681a504 | bibcode=1925JAChS..47.1195H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Everest, A. E.)) | journal=J. Chem. Soc., Trans. | title=XLVIII.—The preparation of diacetonamine | volume=115 | pages=588–592 | date= 1919 | doi=10.1039/CT9191500588}}</ref><ref name=Syntheses>{{cite journal | journal=Organic Syntheses | title=Diacetonamine Hydrogen Oxalate | volume=6 | pages=28 | date= 1926 | doi=10.15227/orgsyn.006.0028}}</ref><ref name=Class> (Experiment '''8''' & '''12''') [https://archive.org/details/classbookoforgan030530mbp/mode/2up A Class-Book of Organic Chemistry, by J. B. Cohen, 12, 1919.]</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Sokoloff, N.)), ((Latschinoff, P.)) | journal=Berichte der Deutschen Chemischen Gesellschaft | title=Ueber die Einwirkung des Ammoniaks auf Aceton | volume=7 | issue=2 | pages=1384–1387 | date= July 1874 | doi=10.1002/cber.187400702137}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Ôeda, H.)) | journal=Bulletin of the Chemical Society of Japan | title=ACTION OF LIQUID AMMONIA UPON ACETOONE COMPOUNDS OF α-HYDROXY-ACIDS | volume=11 | issue=6 | pages=385–389 | date=1 June 1936 | doi=10.1246/bcsj.11.385}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Heintz, W.)) | journal=Justus Liebigs Annalen der Chemie | title=Rückverwandlung des Triacetonamins in Diacetonamin und eine fünfte Acetonbasis | volume=181 | issue=1 | pages=70–89 | date= January 1876 | doi=10.1002/jlac.18761810107}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Son, P.-N.)), ((Lai, J. T.)) | journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry | title=Synthesis of hexahydro-3,3,5,5,7-pentaalkyl-2H-1,4-diazepin-2-ones from 1,3-diamines and ketones | volume=46 | issue=2 | pages=323–327 | date= January 1981 | doi=10.1021/jo00315a020}}</ref> Mesityl oxide itself is formed from the dehydration of [[diacetone alcohol]].<ref>{{cite journal | journal=Organic Syntheses | title=MESITYL OXIDE | volume=1 | pages=53 | date= 1921 | doi=10.15227/orgsyn.001.0053}}</ref> However, it can also be prepared directly from acetone without isolating the intermediate alcohol.
[[File:Diacetonamine synthesis.svg|Diacetonamine synthesis.svg|center|400px]]
It is claimed that diacetonamine can also be prepared by the direct reaction between ammonia and acetone.<ref name=Class/><ref name=Syntheses/> However, closer inspection of the literature reveals that different products are obtained from this reaction.<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Patterson, T. S.)), ((McMillan, A.)) | journal=J. Chem. Soc., Trans. | title=XXXIII.—The action of ammonia on acetone | volume=119 | pages=269–271 | date= 1921 | doi=10.1039/CT9211900269}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors=((Bradbury, R. B.)), ((Hancox, N. C.)), ((Hatt, H. H.)) | journal=J. Chem. Soc. | title=261. The reaction between acetone and ammonia : the formation of pyrimidine compounds analogous to the aldoxans of späth | volume=0 | pages=1394–1399 | date= 1947 | doi=10.1039/JR9470001394}}</ref>
